correction.text: Dakshina Kosala (Chhattisgarh), Kalinga-raja's Tummana near Bilaspur

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Ratnapura row). "The Ratnapura branch was established by Kalinga-raja around 1000 CE ... He made Tummana (near modern-day Bilaspur) his capital." The branch "ruled as vassals of the parent dynasty for many years" (Tripuri). The page gives no area; the 120 km radius round Bilaspur is the researcher's reading of Dakshina Kosala.

correction.text: Dakshina Kosala round Bilaspur and southern Kosala (the Raipur plain), without Bastar

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; review fix 2026-10-19: was all of Chhattisgarh outside the Bilaspur disc, including Bastar. "In 1114 CE, Jajalla-deva I invaded the Chindaka Naga territory to the south", "defeated the Chindaka Naga king Somesvara and took him prisoner" and annexed "southern parts of Kosala which were under Telugu Choda governorship". The page names no place for either, and does not say he annexed the Naga country (Somesvara was released), so the Chindaka Naga land (Bastar) is not drawn; southern Kosala is read as the Raipur plain (120 km round Raipur inside Chhattisgarh). 133 cells of the former shape also lay in kakatiya-dynasty's 1177-1225 shape; the new one has 3. 1226-1739 is a bridge (confidence 1): the page says "No information is available about Pratapamalla's successors", that the kingdom "was unaffected by the Muslim invasions of the 13th-16th centuries" and "enjoyed 700 years of peaceful existence", and that "The next Kalachuri inscriptions are from the reign of the 15th-16th century king Vahara"; a theory has the Eastern Ganga king Anangabhima-deva III defeat Pratapa-malla (uncertain). The shape is kept unchanged because no page gives a change. No infobox area.

correction.text: unchanged shape; the kingdom accepts the suzerainty of the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "The Ratanpur kingdom accepted the suzerainty of the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom in 1740" after Bhaskar Pant's invasion; "The kingdom survived until 1758, when its last ruler Mohan Singh died" and Nagpur annexed it. The shape is unchanged (status only: a vassal of Nagpur, to be drawn as the lighter tint from the Maratha side; maratha-empire should carry vassal_start 1740 and vassal_end 1758 with counterpart kalachuris-of-ratnapura). The page gives no extent for these years.

region.text: Dakshina Kosala (Chhattisgarh), Kalinga-raja's Tummana near Bilaspur

ledger.note: c. 1000: Kalinga-raja sets up the Ratnapura branch at Tummana. "The Ratnapura branch was established by Kalinga-raja around 1000 CE." He conquered Dakshina Kosala from the Somavamshi dynasty; the branch were "an offshoot of the Kalachuris of Tripuri" and vassals of them for many years.

1114: Jajalla-deva I annexes southern Kosala. "In 1114 CE, Jajalla-deva I invaded the Chindaka Naga territory to the south" and annexed "southern parts of Kosala which were under Telugu Choda governorship"; the Chindaka Naga king Somesvara was defeated and taken prisoner (see the war), the Naga country itself is not said to be annexed. Review fix 2026-10-19: counterpart narrowed to the governors; the region, which was all of Chhattisgarh outside the Bilaspur disc, is the Raipur plain (the page names no place), so confidence 2.
1740: "the general of the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom, Bhaskar Pant invaded the kingdom." The page gives no battle or land taken.
1740: "The Ratanpur kingdom accepted the suzerainty of the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom in 1740." The vassal tint 1740-1758 belongs to the Maratha dossier (vassal_start with this kingdom as counterpart).

region.text: the Ratanpur kingdom, annexed by its suzerain

ledger.note: 1758: "The kingdom survived until 1758, when its last ruler Mohan Singh died" and the state was annexed by its suzerain, the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom (infobox: "Bimbaji Bhonsle becomes governor of Chhattisgarh: 1758"). Review fix 2026-10-19: replaces the 1225 dissolve to nobody, which the page does not support.

wars.name: Jajalla-deva I against the Chindaka Nagas
wars.outcome: "Jajalla-deva I defeated the Chindaka Naga king Somesvara and took him prisoner"; his release followed his mother's intervention; the same year southern Kosala was annexed from the Telugu Choda governors. No Naga land is said to be annexed.
wars.note: The page names no places; Bastar is not drawn.

wars.name: Ratna-deva II against the Eastern Ganga
wars.outcome: Ratna-deva II repulsed an invasion by Anantavarman Chodaganga; the page describes "a long conflict for the control of the Trikalinga and Kosala regions".
wars.note: No year on the page; the span is the reign Ratna-deva II is listed with (1120-1135).

wars.name: Ratnapura independence from Tripuri
wars.outcome: Ratna-deva II "officially declared independence from the Kalachuris of Tripuri"; Gayakarna's army sent against him "was defeated".
wars.note: Dated by the overlap of Gayakarna's reign (c. 1123-1153) and Ratna-deva II's (1120-1135); the Tripuri dossier has the matching vassal_end.

wars.name: Maratha invasion of the Ratanpur kingdom
wars.outcome: Bhaskar Pant invaded and the kingdom accepted the suzerainty of the Maratha Nagpur Kingdom; annexed in 1758 on the death of Mohan Singh.
wars.note: No battle, route or land taken on the page.

certainty.note: No frontier is given on the page; Dakshina Kosala (Bilaspur) and southern Kosala are the only places it names, and 1226-1739 has no information at all.

notes: Cliopatria has no Ratnapura row. Two pages; the Ratnapura page lists rulers only to 1225 with estimated years. Review fixes 2026-10-19: (1) the state now runs to 1758, as the page says ("The kingdom survived until 1758"): 1226-1739 is a confidence-1 bridge with the shape unchanged (the page: "No information is available about Pratapamalla's successors"; next inscriptions under Vahara, 15th-16th century), the 1740 Maratha invasion and acceptance of Nagpur's suzerainty are a contest pair in one year plus a war, and the dissolve of 1758 goes to maratha-empire (confidence 3); maratha-empire (whoever writes it) should carry the vassal tint 1740-1758 and the gain of 1758. (2) The 1114 gain is the Raipur plain (southern Kosala), not all of Chhattisgarh: the page names no place, and Bastar (the Chindaka Naga country) is not said to be annexed; the counterpart is the Telugu Choda governors and the Nagas are a separate war. 3 cells now overlap kakatiya-dynasty's 1177-1225 shape (133 before). Disagreements with the reviewer: none. Not settled: where the Telugu Choda governors held southern Kosala and what the Kalachuris held in 1226-1739 (the page gives no extent; a gap-filler should open the Ratanpur / Haihayas of Chhattisgarh articles, which may carry the rulers of the 14th-18th centuries). The c. 1000 loss to this state is now in somavamshi-dynasty (/ledger/2). Independence from Tripuri is not a ledger type; it is recorded as a war and as the vassal_end in the kalachuris-of-tripuri dossier. Gazetteer lacks Tummana, Ratanpur.
